passage: I'm Yamini. On Tuesdays I pick up my little brother Ramesh from nursery. Today I came early and watched through the window. He was stacking cups, happy. Then a girl beside him dropped her biscuit and wailed. Ramesh looked at her. His lip wobbled. Then he wailed too, even louder, though nothing had happened to him. Two more babies joined in. The teacher picked him up. I don't know what he was feeling. Maybe her crying just got inside him.

qa.q: What was Ramesh doing before the girl began to wail?
qa.a: Stacking cups, happy.

qa.q: What might have made Ramesh cry when nothing had happened to him?
qa.a: Ramesh may have simply caught the other child's upset; very young children can feel another's crying almost as their own.

qa.q: The teacher picked Ramesh up. What else could help when crying spreads like this?
qa.a: Calmly comforting the first crying child as well can settle the others quickly, since the feeling started there.

qa.q: How does Yamini understand what happened to Ramesh?
qa.a: Yamini isn't sure, but thinks the girl's crying got inside Ramesh, a child's way of noticing that feelings spread.

grounding: An older sibling sees a toddler brother burst into tears when another child cries at nursery.

passage: In the daycare above the chemist's shop in Lajpat Nagar, nap time was nearly over. Jatin, eighteen months, sat on his mat sucking his thumb, sleepy and calm. Then Ramesh, on the next mat, woke with a start and screamed. Jatin's thumb popped out. He stared at Ramesh, chin trembling, and burst into tears, arms out for the caregiver. Soon three mats were crying. The caregiver scooped up Ramesh first, rocking and humming. As Ramesh quietened, Jatin's sobs slowed too, and he crawled closer to pat Ramesh's foot.

qa.q: Where was the daycare?
qa.a: Above the chemist's shop in Lajpat Nagar.

qa.q: Why did Jatin burst into tears when he had been sleepy and calm?
qa.a: Jatin seemed to catch Ramesh's sudden upset; seeing and hearing Ramesh scream made Jatin upset too.

qa.q: The caregiver comforted Ramesh first. Why was that a good choice?
qa.a: Calming the child who started it helped stop the crying from spreading, and Jatin settled as Ramesh quietened.

qa.q: How might Ramesh feel when Jatin pats Ramesh's foot?
qa.a: Ramesh, just woken and frightened, might feel a little comforted by a friendly touch from the next mat.

grounding: A calm toddler bursts into tears when another child wakes screaming, and settles as that child is soothed.

Nursery note, Thursday. Rekha, Butterfly Room.
Omkar was pouring water at the tub. Tushar tripped near the shoe rack and cried. Omkar dropped his cup, stared, and cried too, big tears, though nothing had happened to him.
I held Tushar and sat beside Omkar so both could lean on me, singing the boat song. Tushar quietened first; Omkar watched him, hiccuped, stopped.
Next: telling Omkar's mother at pickup. Little ones catch each other's tears. 🙂

qa.q: What song did Rekha sing?
qa.a: Rekha sang the boat song.

qa.q: What does Omkar's crying suggest about how he felt when Tushar tripped?
qa.a: It suggests Omkar felt upset simply because Tushar was upset; the feeling spread to him even though nothing had happened to him.

qa.q: Which of Rekha's choices worked well, and why?
qa.a: Sitting with both boys together and singing the boat song worked, because once Tushar calmed, Omkar could see it and calm down too.

qa.q: How might Omkar's mother react if she reads this note?
qa.a: She would probably feel reassured, knowing that if Omkar seems upset for no clear reason, it may be because he caught another child's tears.

grounding: It shows a toddler at nursery crying as soon as another child cries, with feelings spreading quickly between very young children.

"Why is Parul crying? She was just laughing," Anjali's father asked at the nursery gate, winter coats piled on the bench.
"Her friend fell off the rocking horse," the teacher said. "He cried, and Parul started a second later."
"But she isn't hurt?"
"No. Little ones catch it from each other. When one starts, the whole row can go."
Parul wailed, "Ow! Ow!" and held her own knee.
"See? She feels it too, poor thing."
Anjali, still in her mittens, patted Parul's head. "Shh, baby."

qa.q: What did Parul's friend fall off?
qa.a: He fell off the rocking horse.

qa.q: Why does Parul hold her own knee and cry 'Ow'?
qa.a: She feels upset and distressed because her friend cried; his hurt feeling spread to her even though she is not hurt.

qa.q: How could the nursery staff help when crying spreads through the room?
qa.a: They could comfort the hurt child and gently hold or soothe the others nearby, knowing the tears are catching rather than a new injury.

qa.q: How does Anjali's father see Parul's sudden crying?
qa.a: He is confused at first, since she was laughing and is not hurt, until the teacher explains that little ones catch it from each other.

grounding: A toddler cries with a friend who has fallen, holding her own unhurt knee, showing how feelings spread between very young children.
